newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar slumbers in thin market, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: Dollar slumbers in thin market, seen in range.

text.p: The dollar made a sleepy start to the week, easing a notch in thin early Asian trade with most dealers expecting a dull session due to holidays in Tokyo and London.
The pound was also slightly off its opening levels but maintained a positive bias, especially against the mark after a rally in New York trade erased losses in Asia on Friday.
"Sterling's looking pretty good now. And there must be people caught short from Friday," a European bank dealer said.
Dealers said sterling/mark was expected to head back towards the 2.8200-2.8250 region while the lower end of 2.8000 was seen well supported.
The pound was heavily sold in late Asian trade on Friday in reaction to a report in London's The Times newspaper that suggested Britain's new Labour government might adopt a soft pound policy.
But dealers said the British unit would be underpinned by relatively positive fundamentals and expectations of a small interest rate hike.
"There's a lot of anticipation that Labour's going to make an effort to join EMU (European Monetary Union) and that would definitely help the pound," another European bank dealer said.
The dollar was expected to trade a very subdued range of 1.7260-1.7300 marks, with sterling/mark's bid tone expected to provide some support.
"Dollar/yen will probably track dollar/mark. We haven't seen much mark/yen play all morning," the trader said, adding that the dollar was likely to keep to a 126.40-126.80 yen range.
Healthy gains on U.S. stock and bond markets after Friday's release of the April non-farm payrolls report and news of a balanced budget accord would also help the dollar, dealers said.
The U.S. Labor Department reported that payrolls rose 142,000, well below the 211,000 rise expected in a Reuters poll, but the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent -- its lowest reading in 23 years.
